canonical_question: Does the 'point energy-dispersive x-ray spectroscopy analysis' used to verify composition provide sufficient statistical significance for a nearly equiatomic alloy, or was area mapping required?

question_variants.question: Does the 'point energy-dispersive x-ray spectroscopy analysis' used to verify composition provide sufficient statistical significance for a nearly equiatomic alloy, or was area mapping required?
question_variants.resolution_summary: The composition was verified using point energy-dispersive x-ray spectroscopy analysis, yielding specific atomic percentages close to equiatomic, but area mapping details are not provided in the text.

answers.answer: The chemical composition was verified using point energy-dispersive x-ray spectroscopy analysis to be Nb 23.8 Ta 25.5 Ti 24.9 V 25.8, indicating a homogeneous elemental distribution in a nearly equiatomic percentage.
answers.mechanism: Point analysis used to verify composition homogeneity.
answers.boundary_limitation: Method is point analysis, not specified as area mapping.
evidence_spans: The microstructure of the homogenized NbTaTiV refractory HEA was characterized, using the scanning electron microscopy (SEM) backscattered electron (BSE) technique, as shown in Fig. 1A . A typical simple solid-solution HEA microstructure with grain sizes of 200 to 400 μm was identified without the presence of secondary phases or elemental segregations.

The chemical composition of the sample was verified (using the point energy-dispersive x-ray spectroscopy analysis) to be Nb 23.8 Ta 25.5 Ti 24.9 V 25.8 , indicating a homogeneous elemental distribution in a nearly equiatomic percentage.
The measured ND patterns of the bulk samples, as illustrated in Fig. 1B , confirm the single BCC solid solution at RT and elevated temperatures.
